def:limit.title: Limit of a function
def:limit.contentHTML:

0<∣x−x0∣<δ  ⟹  ∣f(x)−L∣<ε.0 < |x - x_0| < \delta \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon.0<∣x−x0​∣<δ⟹∣f(x)−L∣<ε.

def:uniform.title: Uniform continuity
def:uniform.contentHTML:
f:D→Rf : D \to \mathbb{R}f:D→R is uniformly continuous if for every ε>0\varepsilon > 0ε>0 there exists δ>0\delta > 0δ>0 — the same δ\deltaδ for all points — such that

∣x−y∣<δ  ⟹  ∣f(x)−f(y)∣<ε∀ x,y∈D.|x - y| < \delta \implies |f(x) - f(y)| < \varepsilon \qquad \forall\, x, y \in D.∣x−y∣<δ⟹∣f(x)−f(y)∣<ε∀x,y∈D.

rem:uniform-vs-pointwise.contentHTML: Uniform continuity is strictly stronger than continuity: f(x)=x2f(x) = x^2f(x)=x2 is continuous on R\mathbb{R}R but not uniformly continuous, because for any fixed δ\deltaδ the change ∣f(x+δ/2)−f(x)∣=xδ+δ2/4|f(x+\delta/2) - f(x)| = x\delta + \delta^2/4∣f(x+δ/2)−f(x)∣=xδ+δ2/4 grows without bound as x→∞x \to \inftyx→∞. On a bounded domain the distinction disappears (see Theorem 1.14).

thm:compact-uniform.title: Continuous on compact implies uniformly continuous
thm:compact-uniform.contentHTML: If fff is continuous on a closed bounded interval [a,b][a, b][a,b], then fff is uniformly continuous on [a,b][a, b][a,b].

thm:ivt.title: Intermediate Value Theorem
thm:ivt.contentHTML: Let fff be continuous on [a,b][a, b][a,b] and let ccc be any value strictly between f(a)f(a)f(a) and f(b)f(b)f(b). Then there exists x0∈(a,b)x_0 \in (a, b)x0​∈(a,b) such that f(x0)=cf(x_0) = cf(x0​)=c.

cor:ivt-root.title: Existence of roots
cor:ivt-root.contentHTML: If fff is continuous on [a,b][a, b][a,b] and f(a)f(a)f(a) and f(b)f(b)f(b) have opposite signs, then fff has at least one root in (a,b)(a, b)(a,b).
